record.original_question: Find necessary and sufficient conditions under which a skew lattice S can be embedded into a ring as an isomorphic copy of idempotent elements, with the skew-lattice operations represented by ring multiplication and either the quadratic or cubic join. The source lists distributivity, hence categoricity, and cancellativity, hence symmetry, as preconditions, and notes that skew Boolean algebras and their duals, strongly distributive skew lattices, and dual strongly distributive lattices can be embedded. Are there additional sufficient conditions, and what are the complete necessary and sufficient conditions?

evidence.quote: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for a skew lattice S to be embedded into a ring.
That is for S to have an isomorphic copy consisting of idempotents in a ring with the operations being multiplication and either the quadratic or cubic join.
Preconditions include: being distributive (and thus categorical); being cancellative (and thus symmetric).
Clearly skew Boolean algebras and their duals can be embedded into a ring.
More generally, strongly distributive skew lattices [satisfying x∧(y ∨z) = (x∧y)∨(x∧z) and (x ∨ y) ∧ z = (x ∧ z) ∨ (y ∧ z)] and dual strongly distributive lattices can be embedded into a ring.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebra (S, ∧, ∨) where ∧ and ∨ are associative, idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities x ∧ (x ∨ y) = x = x ∨ (x ∧ y) and (x ∧ y) ∨ y = y = (x ∨ y) ∧ y. Given a ring R, its set E(R) of idempotents carries skew-lattice operations defined by e ∧ f = efe·... using ring multiplication for the meet, and either the quadratic join e ∨ f = e + f − ef − fe + efe + fef (cubic join) or e ∨ f = e + f − ef (quadratic join, defined when ef = fe ought not be assumed) — more precisely, when these formulas produce idempotents one obtains skew lattices inside R.

A skew lattice S is said to be embeddable into a ring if there exist a ring R and an injective homomorphism of S onto a sub-skew-lattice of (E(R), ·, ∨) where ∨ is either the quadratic or the cubic join.

Recall: S is distributive if x ∧ (y ∨ z) ∧ x = (x ∧ y ∧ x) ∨ (x ∧ z ∧ x) and the dual identity hold; S is cancellative if x ∨ y = x ∨ z and x ∧ y = x ∧ z imply y = z (and dually); S is symmetric if x ∧ y = y ∧ x ⟺ x ∨ y = y ∨ x; S is categorical if nonempty composites of coset bijections between comparable D-classes are coset bijections. It is known that distributivity (which implies categoricity) and cancellativity (which implies symmetry) are necessary preconditions, and that every skew Boolean algebra, its dual, every strongly distributive skew lattice, and every dual strongly distributive skew lattice can be embedded into a ring in this sense.

Problem: Determine complete necessary and sufficient conditions on a skew lattice S for it to be embeddable into a ring (with meet given by ring multiplication and join given by either the quadratic or cubic join) as a sub-skew-lattice of the idempotents of that ring.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding complete necessary and sufficient conditions for embedding a general skew lattice into a ring as a sub-skew-lattice of idempotents appears to remain open. Known partial results cover skew Boolean algebras, their duals, strongly distributive skew lattices, and (in matrix rings) symmetric normal skew lattices with finite distributive maximal lattice image, but no full characterization has been found.

status_evidence.title: Open problems from NCS 2018
status_evidence.snippet: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for a skew lattice S to be embedded into a ring.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Skew lattice - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Every symmetric, normal skew lattice with a finite, distributive maximal lattice image can be embedded in a skew lattice of upper-triangular matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial embedding results into matrix rings are known, not a complete characterization.
